text: How long have you had this painful ulcerative lesion on your leg, and was there any recent trauma, insect bite, or tick exposure in that area?

speaker: Patient
text: 54-year-old woman. The patient reports a skin lesion on her right leg that has been present for 1 month. The lesion began as a small red spot and has increased in size. She recalls an ant bite at the site before the lesion developed. She has a history of anterior uveitis treated with corticosteroids 8 months ago, as well as Crohn's disease, type 2 diabetes mellitus, and hypertension.

speaker: Doctor
text:
Has the ulcer increased in size rapidly over the last month, and have you noticed any fever, chills, or red streaks radiating from the wound? Additionally, given your history of Crohn's disease and diabetes, have you experienced any recent gastrointestinal symptoms or weight loss?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Painful ulcerative lesion on the right leg. I also have Lesion has a central necrotic base and purplish irregular borders, History of ant bite at the site of the lesion, Pitting pedal edema of the lower extremities, Dilated tortuous veins in both lower legs. A doctor I saw earlier said this was very likely Cellulitis and told me the presentation was already quite typical.

speaker: Doctor
text: Based on the history of antipyrone (ant) bite, your Crohn's disease, diabetes, and the specific description of a lesion with a central necrotic base and purplish borders—which contradicts the typical presentation of cellulitis—I suspect Pyoderma Gangrenosum or a cutaneous vasculitis rather than a simple bacterial infection. REQUEST TEST: HLA-B51, ANCA, and Complement levels (C3, C4). REQUEST IMAGES: Dermatology photograph of the ulcer and lower extremity venous Doppler.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Pyoderma Gangrenosum. Based on the history of antipyrone (ant) bite, your Crohn's disease, diabetes, and the specific description of a lesion with a central necrotic base and purplish borders, this presentation is classic for Pyoderma Gangrenosum, a neutrophilic dermatosis, rather than simple cellulitis or a direct result of the insect bite.
